# 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. Unlike his ancestor David, he did not do what was right in the LORD's eyes.

**2** He followed the ways of the kings of Israel and made cast images for the Baals.

**3** He burned incense in the Valley of Ben Hinnom and sacrificed his own children in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel.

**4** He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hilltops, and under every spreading tree.

**5** So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram. The Arameans defeated him and took large numbers of his people as prisoners to Damascus. He was also given into the hands of the king of Israel, who inflicted heavy casualties on him.

**6** In a single day, Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 soldiers in Judah — all brave men — because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

**7** Zichri, an Ephraimite warrior, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the palace commander, and Elkanah, who was second to the king.

**8** The Israelites took 200,000 captives from their own relatives — women, sons, and daughters — and also seized a large amount of plunder, which they took back to Samaria.

**9** But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there in Samaria. He went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and said, "The LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah and gave them into your hands. But you slaughtered them in a rage that reaches to heaven.

**10** And now you plan to enslave the people of Judah and Jerusalem? Don't you have sins of your own against the LORD your God?

**11** Listen to me! Send the prisoners back — they are your own relatives! The LORD's fierce anger hangs over you."

**12** Then some Ephraimite leaders — Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai — confronted the returning army.

**13** "Don't bring those captives here!" they said. "You're only adding to our sins and guilt. Our guilt is already enormous, and the LORD's fierce anger is on Israel."

**14** So the soldiers gave up the captives and plunder to the officials and the whole assembly.

**15** Designated men took charge of the prisoners. From the plunder, they provided clothes for all who were naked. They dressed them, gave them sandals, food, and drink, and put ointment on their wounds. They put the weak ones on donkeys and took them all to Jericho, the City of Palms, near their own people. Then they returned to Samaria.

**16** At that time King Ahaz asked the king of Assyria for help.

**17** The Edomites had again attacked Judah and carried away prisoners.

**18** The Philistines had also raided towns in the foothills and the Negev of Judah, capturing Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, along with their surrounding villages, and settled in them.

**19** The LORD had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, who had encouraged moral decline in Judah and had been completely unfaithful to the LORD.

**20** Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came to him, but he gave him trouble instead of help.

**21** Ahaz took some things from the LORD's temple and from the royal palace and from the officials, and gave them to the king of Assyria — but it did no good.

**22** In his time of trouble, King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD.

**23** He offered sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him. He thought, "Since the gods of the kings of Aram helped them, I'll sacrifice to them so they'll help me too." But they became his downfall — and the downfall of all Israel.

**24** Ahaz gathered up the articles from God's temple and smashed them. He shut the doors of the LORD's temple and set up altars on every street corner in Jerusalem.

**25** In every town in Judah he built high places to burn incense to foreign gods, provoking the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.

**26** Everything else he did and all his ways, from first to last, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

**27** Ahaz rested with his ancestors and was buried in the city of Jerusalem — but not in the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah succeeded him.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **28:3**: Ahaz burns his own children as sacrifices. The Chronicler states it without comment — the horror speaks for itself. This is where abandoning God ultimately leads.

- **28:15**: One of the most beautiful scenes in the Bible: northern Israelites clothing, feeding, and caring for their Judean prisoners — enemies treating enemies with radical compassion. Jesus will tell a similar story about a Samaritan centuries later.

- **28:23**: "Since their gods helped them, I'll sacrifice to them too." The logic of desperation. Ahaz doesn't worship these gods because he believes in them — he worships them because they seem to work. And they destroy him. Pragmatic idolatry is still idolatry.

- **28:24**: Ahaz shuts the doors of God's temple. Let that image sit with you. The king of Judah locks God out of God's own house. This is the anti-Solomon, the undoing of everything chapters 1-7 built.


— PNEUMA
